OpenSSF silver certified: fewer than 1% of open source projects reach this level.

> [!NOTE] > Native agent tools (regex search, path matching, file reading) handle targeted lookups well. `aptu-coder` handles the mechanical, non-AI work: mapping directory structure and extracting symbols, so a coding agent's context window is spent reasoning instead of re-deriving structure on every call. Most code-intelligence tooling for AI agents indexes a codebase into a cloud embedding or vector store and retrieves by similarity search. aptu-coder instead parses the codebase on-device with tree-sitter and serves it locally over MCP: no source code leaves the machine, and retrieval is exact (symbol tables) rather than approximate (nearest-neighbor similarity). ## Benchmarks Paired comprehension tasks on Claude Code (MCP mode vs native shell search). Methodology: [Django](https://github.com/django/django) auth migration ([v12](https://github.com/clouatre-labs/aptu-coder/blob/main/docs/benchmarks/v12/methodology.md)) and [OpenFAST](https://github.com/OpenFAST/openfast) AeroDyn integration audit ([v13](https://github.com/clouatre-labs/aptu-coder/blob/main/docs/benchmarks/v13/methodology.md)). | Task | Mode | Sonnet 4.6 | Haiku 4.5 | Savings | |---|---|---|---|---| | Django (Python) | MCP | 112k tokens, $0.39 | 406k tokens, $0.42 | **59% fewer tokens, 59% cheaper** (Sonnet) | | Django (Python) | Native | 276k tokens, $0.95 | 473k tokens, $0.53 | 14% fewer tokens, 21% cheaper (Haiku) | | OpenFAST (Fortran) | MCP | 472k tokens, $1.65 | 687k tokens, $0.72 | **46% fewer tokens, 42% cheaper** (Sonnet) | | OpenFAST (Fortran) | Native | 877k tokens, $2.85 | 2162k tokens, $2.21 | **68% fewer tokens, 68% cheaper** (Haiku) | A real end-to-end multi-agent run against this repository itself: five refactoring issues (#1578–#1582) fixed by the [coder skill](https://github.com/clouatre-labs/agentic-coder-skill) in one orchestrated session — 23 subagent spawns (5 scout, 1 guard, 10 build, 7 check), ~1h42m, three human interventions — producing PRs #1584–#1588, all merged with CI green. Recommended uses: premise grounding for multi-agent workflows, and non-agentic MCP consumers (IDE assistants, CI jobs, scoring pipelines). ## Overview

*Figure 1: An AI agent connects over MCP to aptu-coder, whose analyze tools feed tree-sitter parsing into the formatter.* aptu-coder is a comprehension layer for coding agents: it gives an agent harness precise structural context about a codebase, directory trees, and symbol definitions, without the agent reading raw files or re-deriving structure on every call. That prevents context starvation on large or unfamiliar codebases while keeping the result set small enough to fit the model's context window. It supports 18 languages (see [Supported Languages](#supported-languages)) and integrates with any MCP-compatible orchestrator. ### class_declaration fields in node-types.json

Source: https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-php/blob/master/php/src/node-types.json

### class_declaration rule definition

Source: https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-php/blob/master/common/define-grammar.js

The grammar rule for class_declaration: it defines the field 'name' (plus 'attributes' and 'body'), and uses optional base_clause (extends) and class_interface_clause (implements) nodes instead of parent_class/base_classes/interfaces fields. Method declarations appear inside the body's declaration_list, and functions are named function_definition in this grammar.

```javascript
      class_declaration: $ => prec.right(seq(
        optional(field('attributes', $.attribute_list)),
        repeat($._modifier),
        keyword('class'),
        field('name', reserved('classes', $.name)),
        optional($.base_clause),
        optional($.class_interface_clause),
        field('body', $.declaration_list),
```

Demonstrates how to use the tree-sitter-php crate to parse PHP code. It initializes a tree-sitter parser, sets the PHP language, and parses a sample PHP string. Asserts that the parsed tree does not contain errors.

```rust
let code = r#"<?php
  echo "Hello, World!";

let language = tree_sitter_php::LANGUAGE_PHP;
parser

let tree = parser.parse(code, None).unwrap();
assert!(!tree.root_node().has_error());
```
